title: Land Use Regulations
overview: How government and private parties limit land use: the four government powers (PETE), New York planning and zoning, variances, nonconforming uses, subdivisions, building codes, SEQR, wetlands, eminent domain and deed restrictions. The exam hits classification (police power or eminent domain? use or area variance?), New York procedure (who decides, which deadline, how many votes) and short calculations.

mustKnow: **PETE**: police power, eminent domain, taxation, escheat. Only **eminent domain** pays the owner.
**Police power** (health, safety, morals, welfare) supports zoning, codes, subdivision rules and rent regulation. A valid rule owes **no compensation**, even if value drops.
**Eminent domain** requires public use and **just compensation**: fair market value at highest and best use. Condemnation is the process. No owner consent is needed.
**Escheat**: the State takes property of an owner who dies with no will and no heirs. **Tax foreclosure** is taxation, not eminent domain.
Only the elected **legislative body** adopts or amends zoning. The **ZBA cannot rezone**.
Zoning must follow the **comprehensive plan**, which the legislative body adopts. Until a rezoning, the **current zoning controls**.
**Planning board** (appointed): plats, site plans, cluster plans, often special permits. **ZBA** (quasi-judicial): appeals, interpretations, variances.

**Use variance** needs **unnecessary hardship**: no reasonable return from every permitted use, shown by competent financial evidence; a unique hardship; no change to neighborhood character; not self-created.
**Area variance** uses a **balancing test**: benefit vs detriment, five factors. Self-created difficulty counts but is not fatal.
Variances: the ZBA grants the **minimum** relief and may add land-related conditions. A variance **runs with the land**.
A **special use permit** approves a use the ordinance already allows once standards are met. **No hardship** showing is needed. The legislative body designates the issuing board.

A **lawful nonconforming use** **survives a sale**. It generally cannot expand, switch to another nonconforming use, or resume after the discontinuance period, whatever the intent. Amortization can end it.
**Spot zoning** (small parcel, owner's benefit, against the plan) is invalid. A small rezoning that **follows the plan** is valid.
A **protest** by owners of 20% of the land, or of land within 100 feet, means a rezoning needs **three-fourths** of the town board.
ZBA timeline: appeal within 60 days; decision within 62 days after the hearing. Any action needs a **majority of the full board**.
Challenge a ZBA decision by an **Article 78** proceeding in Supreme Court within **30 days** of its filing with the town clerk. A rational decision stands.
**Subdivision**: the planning board approves the plat. File the signed plat with the county clerk within **62 days**. A performance bond can secure unbuilt improvements.
**Cluster** = same density on smaller lots. **PUD** = mixed uses under one plan.
**Incentive zoning** = bonus for amenities. **TDR** = development rights moved to a receiving area.
A **building permit** authorizes construction. A **certificate of occupancy** authorizes occupancy for the stated use; a use change needs an amended CO.
Outside NYC, the **Uniform Code** sets minimums. Stricter local rules need Code Council approval, and code variances go to DOS **regional boards of review**.
NYC has its own codes, enforced by its Department of Buildings (DOB).
**SEQR** covers **discretionary** agency actions; ministerial acts are excluded.
SEQR types: **Type I** (Full EAF, EIS likelier), **Type II** (no review), Unlisted (everything else).
SEQR order: EAF → negative or positive declaration → draft EIS and comment → final EIS → findings.
DEC (freshwater and tidal), localities and the Army Corps (§404) may all regulate a wetland, including its **adjacent areas**. Get a current **jurisdictional determination**.
The **Adirondack Park Agency (APA)** controls private land in the Park: Hamlet is densest, Resource Management strictest. Forest Preserve land is **forever wild**.
**Inverse condemnation** = owner sues over a de facto taking. A partial taking adds **severance damages**.
**Covenants** bind later owners through recording. The **stricter** of zoning or covenant controls, and a variance doesn't release a covenant.
A deed **condition** with a right of re-entry can forfeit title. Covenant breach brings an injunction or damages.
**Laches** can bar slow enforcers. **Discriminatory covenants** are unenforceable (Shelley v. Kraemer).
The federal **ILSFDA** requires a **property report** before signing. The buyer can revoke within 7 days, or 2 years if no report was given.
**RPL Article 9-A**: installment sales of vacant subdivided land to NY residents need a DOS filing. Buyers may cancel within 7 days.

traps.trap: A zoning change that lowers my land's value entitles me to compensation.
traps.truth: Zoning is police power. Compensation is owed only for eminent domain or a regulation so severe it becomes a taking.

traps.trap: The ZBA can rezone a street to match the comprehensive plan.
traps.truth: Rezoning is legislative (town board, village board, city council). The plan guides; the current zoning controls until amended.

traps.trap: A self-created problem kills any variance.
traps.truth: It bars a use variance, but for an area variance it is only one factor in the balancing test.

traps.trap: Showing a store would earn more, or that the current use loses money, proves hardship.
traps.truth: The owner must show, with competent financial evidence, no reasonable return from every permitted use.

traps.trap: A special use permit is a variance granted by the ZBA after proof of hardship.
traps.truth: It approves a use the ordinance already allows if standards are met. No hardship; the issuing board is often the planning board.

traps.trap: A nonconforming use ends when the property is sold.
traps.truth: It runs with the land. It ends through discontinuance, amortization or destruction rules, and generally cannot expand or switch to another nonconforming use. Older textbooks (including Spada) say a sale ends it.

traps.trap: The owner always meant to reopen, so the discontinued nonconforming use survives.
traps.truth: Once the ordinance's discontinuance period runs, the right is lost regardless of intent (Toys "R" Us v. Silva).

traps.trap: You have 4 months to sue over a ZBA decision.
traps.truth: 30 days from filing with the town clerk. Four months is the general Article 78 limit; 60 days is the appeal to the ZBA.

traps.trap: A 3–2 vote of the five members present passes on a seven-member ZBA.
traps.truth: A majority of the full board is required: 4 of 7.

traps.trap: A building permit lets the buyer move in once the house is framed.
traps.truth: Occupancy requires a certificate of occupancy (or temporary CO) after inspection.

traps.trap: Every project needs an EIS, and Type I means an automatic EIS.
traps.truth: Only a positive declaration requires an EIS; Type II needs no review and ministerial permits are outside SEQR.

traps.trap: Building on dry ground near a marsh avoids any wetland permit.
traps.truth: Adjacent areas are regulated: 100 feet for freshwater, up to 300 feet (150 in NYC) for tidal wetlands.

traps.trap: A 100-year floodplain floods once a century.
traps.truth: It has a 1% chance every year, about 26% over a 30-year mortgage.

traps.trap: A ZBA variance overrides a stricter recorded covenant.
traps.truth: Both apply and the stricter controls; covenant holders can still sue.

sections.heading: Land-use basics and the four government powers
sections.intro: Ownership gives the bundle of rights (possess, use, exclude, transfer), but every right yields to public regulation and valid private restrictions. For any project, ask: Does zoning allow it? Do other government approvals allow it? Do private restrictions allow it?
points: **Police power** lets government regulate property to protect public health, safety, morals and general welfare. New York delegates it to cities, towns and villages for zoning, building codes and subdivision rules. The State uses it for rules such as rent regulation. A valid regulation owes **no compensation**, even if value drops.
**Eminent domain** takes property for public use with **just compensation**, through condemnation.
**Taxation** includes property taxes and **special assessments** on land that a local improvement, such as a sewer, benefits. Unpaid taxes end in tax foreclosure.
**Escheat** passes property to the State when an owner dies with no will and no heirs. Any qualifying relative, even a first cousin, prevents it.
An **as-of-right** use meets the zoning without a variance or special permit. It still needs a building permit.
New York requires zoning rules to be **uniform** for each kind of building within a district (Town Law §262).

head: Power
What it does
Owner paid?
Example
rows: Regulates use for health, safety and welfare
No, unless it becomes a taking
Raises revenue; liens and tax foreclosure
Takes property with no owner or heir

sections.heading: Planning and the bodies that regulate land use
sections.intro: In New York, land use is mostly local: the elected legislative body makes the rules, appointed boards (the planning board and the zoning board of appeals, or ZBA) apply them, and county and state agencies add layers.
points: The **comprehensive plan** (master plan) sets long-range goals for land use, housing, transportation, utilities and open space.
The plan draws on demography (population statistics), census tracts (small Census Bureau statistical areas), topography (land contours) and infrastructure (roads, water, sewer, schools).
The planning board may draft the plan, but the **legislative body adopts it** (Town Law §272-a).

Zoning must be **in accordance with a comprehensive plan** (Town Law §263). The plan is only a guide: if it calls for shops but the map still says single-family, the **current zoning controls** until the legislative body rezones.

The **official map** shows existing and proposed streets, parks and drainage. In towns, a building permit generally requires access from a street on the official map, an existing public highway or an approved plat (Town Law §280-a).
**Capital budgeting** schedules and funds public improvements.

The **Open Meetings Law** (Sunshine Law) opens planning board, ZBA and legislative meetings to the public, including ZBA deliberations. The **Freedom of Information Law (FOIL)** covers records. Both are New York State laws.
Enforcement runs through the building department or code enforcement officer, the board of health, professional consultants (engineers, surveyors, planners) and the courts.
**Federal Housing Administration (FHA) approval** of homes for FHA-insured loans is a separate federal track.
In NYC, zoning map changes go through the **Uniform Land Use Review Procedure (ULURP)**. The 2025 Charter amendments created the faster **ELURP** for modest housing rezonings.

sections.heading: Zoning districts, bulk rules and key terms
sections.intro: **Zoning** divides a municipality into districts, each with permitted uses and dimensional rules. Towns zone under the Town Law, villages under the Village Law and cities under the General City Law; New York City's 1916 resolution was the nation's first comprehensive zoning code.
points: A zoning law has a **map** (district lines) and **text** (permitted, specially permitted and prohibited uses, plus dimensional rules).
Village of Euclid v. Ambler Realty (1926) upheld use-district zoning as police power, hence the name **Euclidean zoning**.
Classifications include residential, commercial, industrial, agricultural, institutional (schools, hospitals), open space, parks and recreation, vacant land and conservation land.
**Bulk rules** set lot area, frontage, setbacks (minimum distances from lot lines), height, lot coverage, density (units per acre) and parking.
**Floor area ratio (FAR)** = gross floor area ÷ lot area.
**Family** is defined locally. But New York's highest court struck down a definition that excluded households functioning as a family (McMinn v. Town of Oyster Bay, 1985).

A licensed community residence for up to 14 people with mental disabilities counts as a **family unit** (Padavan Law, Mental Hygiene Law §41.34). The municipality has 40 days to approve the site, suggest another or object to over-concentration.

Listing on the State or National Register does not by itself restrict a private owner using private funds; a local landmarks law can. In New York, the **Office of Parks, Recreation and Historic Preservation (OPRHP)** handles listings.

rows: Incidental to the main use on the lot, such as a garage or shed

A resident's business inside the dwelling with little outward sign
Residence for unrelated people who need support; often treated as a family
Right to use another's land for a limited purpose
Easement or strip of land for passage
Dead-end street ending in a turnaround
Right to use the space above land; can be sold separately
Measures boundaries and locates improvements and encroachments

example.title: Worked example: floor area ratio
steps: A 10,000 sq ft lot allows a maximum FAR of 2.0.
Maximum floor area = 10,000 × 2.0 = 20,000 sq ft.
That could be 4 stories of 5,000 sq ft, if height rules allow.
Answer: 20,000 sq ft of floor area.

sections.heading: Zoning techniques
sections.intro: Exam questions describe a flexible zoning tool and ask for its name.
points: **Cluster development**: if the town board authorizes it, the planning board may shrink lots to preserve open space. Total units may **not exceed** a conventional layout (Town Law §278).
A **planned unit development (PUD)** goes further, mixing housing types and commercial uses under one master plan.
**Incentive zoning** trades bonus density or floor area for amenities (Town Law §261-b).
**Transfer of development rights (TDR)** lets owners of preserved land, such as farms or landmarks, sell unused rights for use in a receiving area (Town Law §261-a).
**Inclusionary zoning** requires or rewards affordable units.
**Exclusionary zoning**, such as huge minimum lots, keeps lower-income households out. New York requires zoning to weigh regional housing needs (Berenson v. Town of New Castle, 1975).
**Downzoning** (lowering allowed density) is valid without compensation unless it becomes a taking.

head: Technique
Key idea
rows: Higher uses allowed in lower districts, so a house in a light-industrial zone is fine
Only listed uses, so homes can be barred from industrial zones
Extra rules (historic, flood) laid over base districts; base uses unchanged
In the text but unmapped until applied to a qualifying parcel (Rodgers v. Village of Tarrytown, 1951)
Same density, smaller lots, open space
Mixed uses under one master plan
Development rights moved from a sending to a receiving area

example.title: Worked example: density bonus and affordable split
steps: Base density: 30 acres × 2 units per acre = 60 units.
20% incentive bonus for a park: 60 × 0.20 = 12 extra units.
Total = 60 + 12 = 72 units, not 60 + 20 = 80.
Inclusionary rule: 25% of a 120-unit building = 30 affordable units.
Market-rate units = 120 − 30 = 90.
Answer: 72 units; 90 market-rate units.

sections.heading: Rezoning, spot zoning and moratoriums
sections.intro: Changing the zoning map or text is a **legislative** act of the elected board, taken after a public hearing with at least 10 days' published notice.
points: A rezoning passes by simple majority unless owners file a written **protest**. Qualifying owners hold 20% of the land being changed, or of land within 100 feet of it (adjacent or directly opposite).
After a valid protest, the rezoning needs **three-fourths** of the whole town board (Town Law §265).
Zoning actions within **500 feet** of a municipal boundary, or of a state or county road or park, go to the county planning agency (General Municipal Law §239-m).
If the county recommends disapproval or modification, acting against it takes a **majority plus one** of all members.
**Spot zoning** singles out a small parcel for a different use, mainly for its owner and against the comprehensive plan. It is invalid. A small rezoning that **implements the plan** is valid.
A hardship shared by a whole area, such as highway noise on every lot, calls for **rezoning**, not individual use variances.
A **moratorium** temporarily halts specified development while the town plans or adds capacity; a reasonable one is valid police power and not automatically a taking.

example.title: Worked example: protest-petition vote
steps: A seven-member town board receives a valid protest.
7 × 3/4 = 5.25, rounded up to 6.
Answer: 6 yes votes (a simple majority would be 4).

sections.heading: Variances and special use permits
sections.intro: A **variance** lets one parcel depart from the zoning rules. The ZBA grants two kinds, with different tests (Town Law §267-b). Villages and cities use the same tests. A **special use permit** is not a variance.
points: Classify first. A **use variance** allows a prohibited use, such as a store in a residential zone or a two-family house in a one-family district.

An **area variance** relaxes a dimensional rule for a permitted use: setback, height, lot size, frontage, coverage or parking. Examples: a deck 6 feet into a rear yard, or a house on a 9,000 sq ft lot where 10,000 is required.
**Use variance**: the applicant must prove **unnecessary hardship**, which has four elements.

(1) No reasonable return from **each and every** permitted use, shown by competent financial evidence. Proof that another use would earn more is not enough. The syllabus phrases this as being deprived of all economic use.
(2) The hardship is **unique**, not shared by much of the district. (3) The use won't change the neighborhood's essential character.
(4) The hardship is **not self-created**. Buying with knowledge of the zoning is self-created.

**Area variance**: the ZBA balances benefit to the applicant against detriment to the community. It weighs (1) undesirable change or harm to neighbors, (2) a feasible alternative, (3) substantiality, (4) physical or environmental effects and (5) self-created difficulty.
For an area variance, self-created difficulty counts but is **not fatal**. The syllabus's older label for this test is practical difficulty.

The ZBA grants the **minimum variance** necessary and may impose reasonable, land-related conditions. A variance **runs with the land**, so a condition ending it on sale is invalid (St. Onge v. Donovan, 1988).
A **special use permit** (special exception, conditional use) approves a use the ordinance already lists for the district, once stated standards are met. **No hardship** showing is needed.
The legislative body chooses the issuing board, often the planning board. That board holds a public hearing within 62 days and may add reasonable conditions (Town Law §274-b).

example.title: Worked example: how substantial is an area variance?
steps: A 20-foot side yard is required; the addition would leave 15 feet.
A side yard is a dimensional rule, so this needs an area variance.
Relief = 20 − 15 = 5 feet.
Substantiality = 5 ÷ 20 = 25%. Dividing 5 ÷ 15 = 33% uses the wrong base.
Answer: a 25% area variance, weighed with the other factors.

sections.heading: Nonconforming uses
sections.intro: A **lawful nonconforming use** (grandfathered) was legal before the zoning changed. An **illegal use** was never lawful and gains no protection with age.
points: Nonconforming uses may **continue but not grow**; the goal is to phase them out over time.
Where an ordinance sets a discontinuance period, the right ends when the period runs, **regardless of intent** to reopen (Toys "R" Us v. Silva, 1996).
In NYC the period is **2 continuous years** (Zoning Resolution §52-61).
**Amortization** ends a use after a reasonable period to recover the investment (Harbison v. City of Buffalo, 1958); billboards are typical targets.

head: Situation
General rule
rows: Use continues; it runs with the land
Not allowed on nonconforming status alone
Rebuilding limited by the local ordinance

sections.heading: ZBA procedure and Article 78 review
sections.intro: The ZBA is **administrative and quasi-judicial**: it applies legal standards to individual cases and makes no policy. Its power is mainly **appellate**, so an applicant usually needs a ruling from the zoning officer first.
points: Town and village ZBAs have **3 or 5 members**. A town ZBA that already had 7 when the current law took effect may keep them until the town board reduces it.
Legislative board members cannot serve. Members need **4 hours of training** a year unless the town board waives it.

Any **aggrieved** person may appeal the zoning officer's order or interpretation. The ZBA acts as the ordinance's **interpreter**, for example deciding whether a garage apartment is a prohibited second dwelling.
Every ZBA action needs a **majority of all members**; absences and vacancies count against it. A rehearing instead needs a unanimous vote of the members present.
On an appeal, missing that majority within 62 days is a **default denial**.

**Article 78** of the Civil Practice Law and Rules is the court challenge, brought in State Supreme Court. File within **30 days** after the ZBA decision is filed with the town clerk; the general 4-month Article 78 limit does not apply.
The court upholds a decision with a **rational basis**. It overturns only illegal or **arbitrary and capricious** action.
In NYC the **Board of Standards and Appeals (BSA)** grants variances and hears appeals from DOB zoning rulings.

head: Step
Deadline or rule
rows: 60 days after the zoning officer's determination is filed
Decision filed with the town clerk
Against a county disapproval or modification

example.title: Worked example: counting ZBA votes
steps: A seven-member ZBA; five attend and vote 3–2 to grant.
Needed: a majority of 7 = 4 (5 if the county recommended disapproval or modification).
Answer: not granted, because 3 is a majority of those present, not of the board.

sections.heading: Subdivisions, site plans and land-sale disclosure laws
sections.intro: A **subdivision** divides land into lots for sale or development. When the town board authorizes it, the **planning board** reviews subdivisions (Town Law §§276–278).
points: The developer submits a **plat**: a map of lots, streets, easements, utilities and drainage. It is usually preliminary, then final, with public hearings coordinated with SEQR environmental review.
Final approval is the authorized officer's **signature**; the owner must **file the plat with the county clerk within 62 days** or the approval expires.
Streets, drains and water lines must be built or guaranteed by a **performance bond**. The bond term is up to 3 years unless the board extends it.
If the plat needs recreation land but has no suitable site, the board may require a **fee in lieu of parkland**, held for recreation.
**Site plan review** covers the layout of a permitted use on a site: parking, access, lighting, landscaping and drainage (Town Law §274-a).
**Development costs** (roads, utilities, fees) usually fall on the developer.

Consumer laws apply on top of plat approval: the federal **Interstate Land Sales Full Disclosure Act (ILSFDA)** and New York's **Real Property Law Article 9-A**. The Department of State (DOS) administers Article 9-A.
Since 1997, Article 9-A ads need not be filed with DOS. They must state that the filing is not DOS approval.

example.title: Worked example: maximum lot yield
steps: 30 acres; 25% goes to improvements; 2-acre minimum lots.
Usable land = 30 × 0.75 = 22.5 acres.
Answer: 11 lots. Round down; 30 ÷ 2 = 15 ignores the improvements.

sections.heading: Building codes, permits and certificates of occupancy
sections.intro: Zoning decides what may be built where; **building codes** decide how it must be built. Zoning relief never waives code rules.
points: Outside NYC, the **Uniform Fire Prevention and Building Code** sets statewide **minimums** (Executive Law Article 18). The Energy Code does too. Localities enforce them, or the county or DOS does if a locality opts out.
Stricter local construction standards need State Code Council approval (Executive Law §379). A **code variance** comes from a DOS **regional board of review**, not the ZBA.
**NYC** has its own Construction Codes, enforced by the Department of Buildings (DOB).

A **building permit** authorizes construction before work starts. A **certificate of occupancy (CO)** follows final inspection and permits occupancy for the stated use. It is not a title guarantee or a no-defect warranty.
A CO fixes the legal use and unit count. Converting a two-family to a three-family needs a **new or amended CO**; an extra unit is illegal even if long rented.
NYC began requiring COs in **1938**. Older unchanged buildings may have none, and DOB can issue a Letter of No Objection.

head: Document
When
Meaning
rows: Legal occupancy for the stated use
Change in use, units or egress

sections.heading: SEQR environmental review
sections.intro: The **State Environmental Quality Review Act (SEQR)** makes state and local agencies weigh environmental impacts before approving, funding or undertaking a **discretionary** action, such as a rezoning, subdivision or variance (ECL Article 8; 6 NYCRR Part 617).
points: Review sometimes requires an **environmental impact statement (EIS)**. The Department of Environmental Conservation (DEC) writes the rules. NYC's version is City Environmental Quality Review (CEQR).
**Ministerial** acts, such as a routine building permit issued once fixed standards are met, are outside SEQR (the rules also list them as Type II).

**Type I** actions require the Full EAF (environmental assessment form) and are likelier to need an EIS. Examples: adopting a comprehensive plan or a first comprehensive zoning law, use changes affecting 25+ acres, and a nonresidential project physically altering 10+ acres.
**Type II** actions need no review. All other actions are **Unlisted**.
A **lead agency** coordinates review. If agencies cannot agree on one within 30 days, the DEC Commissioner picks it.
The lead agency issues a negative declaration (no EIS), a conditioned negative declaration (Unlisted actions only) or a **positive declaration** (EIS required).
Amendments effective **June 12, 2026** added environmental-justice review. They also made certain multifamily buildings of up to 10,000 sq ft Type II.
The May 2026 state budget also exempts many housing projects on previously disturbed sites with public water and sewer. Check current rules for a live project.

head: Category
Examples
Result
rows: Comprehensive plan adoption; use changes affecting 25+ acres
Anything not Type I or II
1–3 family home on an approved lot; deck or garage; setback variance; multifamily up to 10,000 sq ft (2026)

example.title: Worked example: SEQR steps in order
steps: The lead agency reviews the EAF.
It issues a positive declaration.
Scoping sets the issues the EIS must cover.
A draft EIS gets at least 30 days of public comment.
A final EIS answers the comments.
At least 10 days later, each agency adopts a findings statement and decides.
Answer: EAF, draft EIS, final EIS, findings.

sections.heading: Wetlands, flood zones, coasts and the Adirondacks
sections.intro: State and federal programs regulate land regardless of local zoning, and they often overlap. Get a **current jurisdictional determination** instead of assuming.
points: **Freshwater wetlands**: DEC regulates the wetland plus a **100-foot adjacent area** (ECL Article 24). Inside the Adirondack Park, the Adirondack Park Agency (APA) regulates wetlands instead.
An April 8, 2026 court decision annulled DEC's 2025 wetland rules. DEC now requires permits for wetlands of **12.4 acres** or more (7.4 acres from 2028) and wetlands it mapped before 2025.

**Tidal wetlands**, such as Long Island salt marshes, need DEC permits (ECL Article 25). The regulated **adjacent area** runs up to 300 feet landward, or 150 feet in NYC, unless a 10-foot contour or a road ends it sooner.
The **U.S. Army Corps of Engineers** issues permits to fill federally regulated wetlands (Clean Water Act §404).
**Coastal Erosion Hazard Areas** need a DEC or approved local permit (ECL Article 34).
A FEMA **Special Flood Hazard Area** (100-year floodplain) has a **1% flood chance every year**.
A mortgage in a flood zone from a federally regulated lender, or a federally backed loan, requires **flood insurance** for the life of the loan. Homeowners policies exclude flood.
The **Adirondack Park Agency** classifies private land in the Park (Executive Law Article 27).

APA classes: **Hamlet** (no density limit), Moderate Intensity (about 1.3 acres per principal building), Low Intensity (3.2), Rural Use (8.5), **Resource Management** (15 buildings per square mile: 640 ÷ 15 ≈ 42.7 acres each) and Industrial Use.

**Forest Preserve** land in the Adirondacks and Catskills is **forever wild**. It cannot be sold, leased or exchanged (NY Constitution Article XIV). The Catskills have no APA; local zoning, DEC and NYC watershed rules apply.

example.title: Worked example: flood risk over a mortgage
steps: Annual flood chance 1%; 30-year mortgage.
No flood in 30 years = 0.99^30 ≈ 0.74.
At least one flood = 1 − 0.74 = 0.26.
Answer: about 26% (not 30%).

sections.heading: Eminent domain, condemnation and takings
sections.intro: The Fifth Amendment and New York Constitution Article I, §7 allow takings only for **public use** with **just compensation**. Takings follow New York's Eminent Domain Procedure Law (EDPL).
points: Condemnors include the State, municipalities, school districts, public authorities and some utilities. No owner consent is needed; refusing an offer affects only the payment.
An owner can challenge the condemnor's published public-use **determination and findings**. The owner must petition the **Appellate Division within 30 days** (EDPL §207).
The condemnor's written offer must be at least its highest approved appraisal (EDPL §303). The owner may take it as an **advance payment** and still claim more (EDPL §304).
A claim against the State goes to the Court of Claims within **3 years** of vesting or the notice of acquisition, whichever is later (EDPL §503). Other condemnors are generally sued in Supreme Court.
**Just compensation** is **fair market value** at highest and best use, not purchase price or assessed value.
A **partial taking** adds **severance damages** for the remainder's lost value.
**Inverse condemnation** is the owner's suit when government effectively takes property without condemning it, such as permanent flooding or constant low flights.

A rule that destroys **all** economic use is generally a taking (Lucas, 1992). Otherwise courts balance impact and expectations. For example, NYC's landmarks law was upheld for Grand Central (Penn Central, 1978).
Kelo v. City of New London (2005) accepted economic development as a public use.

example.title: Worked example: partial taking
steps: Value before $500,000; after $380,000; the strip alone is worth $90,000.
Answer: $120,000; paying only $90,000 ignores the remainder's loss.

sections.heading: Private land-use controls
sections.intro: Private restrictions apply alongside zoning. The owner must satisfy both, so the **stricter** rule controls.
points: A **deed restriction** or restrictive covenant is a recorded limit on use, such as single-family only, setbacks or design approval. Subdivisions often record **covenants, conditions and restrictions (CC&Rs)**, enforced by a homeowners association (HOA).
Recording gives **constructive notice**, so later owners are bound even if they never read the restrictions.
Covenant breach brings an **injunction or damages** from benefited owners.
A deed **condition** with a right of re-entry (fee simple subject to a condition subsequent) can cost the owner **title**.
A ZBA variance or building permit **does not release** a covenant: the municipality enforces zoning, while private parties enforce covenants.
Covenants end by expiration, release, merger, or a court finding of no real benefit because of **changed conditions** (RPAPL §1951).
Under the **doctrine of laches**, owners who unreasonably delay enforcement may lose the right.
**Discriminatory covenants** are unenforceable (**Shelley v. Kraemer**, 1948) and banned by fair housing laws, however old the deed.
